images.title: A square turned on its corner
images.purpose: Show that a square keeps its sides and angles when turned until it stands on a corner.
images.composition: Two squares side by side with wide space, flat on the left and the same square turned on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one square of side 3 cm in teal #0072B2 lying flat, 1 tick mark on each of the 4 sides, a small right-angle sign at each corner. Right: the same square turned 45 degrees so it stands on one corner, also teal, 1 tick mark on each side, a right-angle sign at each corner. A small grey #6B7280 curved arrow between them. Exactly 2 squares.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Turning a square does not change its sides or angles.
images.description: A flat teal square and the same square turned 45 degrees on one corner, both with equal tick marks and right angle signs, joined by a curved arrow.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one side and one corner in both squares and say what stayed the same.

image_decisions.why: The before and after pair makes the idea.
